descriptions.rgb: Across all five frames, the camera looks steeply downward onto a dirt enclosure bordered by a chain-link fence, with a narrow water channel or wet area visible beyond the fence. One person stands roughly 2–3 metres in front of and below the camera wearer, generally facing toward the wearer with their head angled downward or partly turned; they shift from the left side of view toward the centre and then the right as the viewpoint moves. A dark pile or object lies on the ground about 1–2 metres to the person’s right in the earlier frames, while a cluster of rocks enters near the lower-right foreground in the middle frames and later shifts leftward relative to the image. The person remains about 1–2 metres from the fence, and the scattered ground objects are roughly 1–3 metres apart from one another; none is clearly within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach. The lower edge cuts off nearby foreground and intermittently clips the person’s feet or legs, while fence posts and terrain beyond the fence are partly out of view; over time the apparent lateral motion is stronger than any clear approach or retreat.
